description: Source-lore pass 11 imports nine Kaysender character backgrounds, preserving their setting identity and isolating 5e proficiencies, equipment, and features as legacy mechanics.

entries.title: Skyfarer Background
entries.summary: Skyfarers grow up aboard airships or in airborne communities and read winds, weather, and aerial hazards as naturally as others read roads.
body: Skyfarers are raised among crews, turbulent winds, and the unpredictable dangers of floating-island travel. They know the skies intimately and often regard their first crew as family.
Their outlook prizes freedom and open horizons. Many collect stories for stars and currents, distrust prolonged life on solid ground, and become uneasy when no vessel is near.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Acrobatics and Perception, navigator's tools, airship vehicles, a route map, skycompass, rope harness, 10 gp, and Eye of the Storm, which predicts aerial weather and anomalies one day ahead. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Abyss Watcher Background
entries.summary: Abyss Watchers guard settlements at the edge of the Eternal Abyss and remain alert for creatures, traps, and magical dangers rising from below.
body: Abyss Watchers spend their lives holding the boundary between settled skylands and the dangers of the Eternal Abyss. Duty, vigilance, and loss shape them; many have seen consequences that distant people cannot understand.
They scan constantly for overlooked threats, take pride in holding the line, and may distrust anyone who has never faced the abyss directly.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Athletics and Survival, a fortification- or trap-related artisan tool, boots, etched skystone, hunting trap, 8 gp, and Abyssal Warning for detecting abyssal creatures, traps, and magic. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Driftlander Background
entries.summary: Driftlanders come from isolated drifting islands where self-sufficiency, careful foraging, simplicity, and distrust of waste are necessary for survival.
body: Driftlanders grow up far from crowded mainlands and bustling skyports. Isolation teaches them to forage, make do with limited resources, and protect the small island communities they call home.
They tend to value simplicity and self-reliance, remain curious but wary of the wider world, and may distrust technologies or magic absent from their upbringing.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Nature and Insight, herbalism and an artisan tool, dried herbs, a charm, sky-fishing net, 5 gp, and Island Resilience for finding food and water for a small group on non-barren islands. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Guild Artisan of the Sky Trade
entries.summary: Sky-trade guild artisans craft essential goods and depend on professional reputation, guild resources, workshops, allies, and safe havens.
body: Guild artisans are trained inside organizations that supply goods and services essential to airborne life. Their identity is tied to craft quality, efficiency, competition, and the honor or reputation of their guild.
Membership opens workshops, resources, business relationships, and safe havens across the trade network, but those benefits depend on maintaining standing with fellow members.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Persuasion and Investigation, artisan tools, airship or seafaring vehicles, tools, guild certificate, ledger, 15 gp, and Guild Connections. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Sky Reclaimer Background
entries.summary: Sky Reclaimers salvage abandoned ruins, fallen ships, and forgotten islands for artifacts, components, maps, and resources.
body: Sky Reclaimers search wreckage, ruins, and forgotten islands for things the skies have swallowed. They keep battered journals of maps and notes, recognize value where others see debris, and accept risks in pursuit of the next great find.
A life of salvage creates both expertise and temptation: Reclaimers can identify valuable components quickly, but many struggle to leave a promising danger unexplored.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Sleight of Hand and History, thieves' and tinker's tools, tools, crowbar, journal, 7 gp, and Treasure Hunter's Instinct for identifying valuable objects in ruins and wreckage. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Skybound Noble Background
entries.summary: Skybound Nobles come from families that rule islands, control trade fleets, or serve as vassals to Dragon Lords.
body: Skybound Nobles inherit status from families tied to island rule, major fleets, or service beneath [[dragon-lords|Dragon Lords]]. Their crests and names open high society, guild halls, and political audiences unavailable to common travelers.
The background carries responsibility as well as privilege. Some nobles embrace the duty to protect dependents; others become isolated from people of lower status or obsessed with family honor.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants History and Intimidation, calligrapher's supplies, airship vehicles, a crested cloak, signet ring, tools, 25 gp, and Noble Influence for securing audiences with minor Dragon Lords and guild leaders. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Guild Apprentice Background
entries.summary: Guild Apprentices retain the training, habits, insignia, workshop access, and relationships of a current or former guild life.
body: Guild Apprentices learn a craft, trade, or technical discipline under an established organization. Whether still loyal or long departed, they carry their mentors' standards, compare themselves to past instruction, and remain marked by guild habits and relationships.
Their affiliation can provide workshops and professional aid, but guild reputation is reciprocal: disgrace or betrayal can close the same doors membership once opened.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Arcana and Insight, an artisan tool or trade kit, tools, insignia, ledger, 10 gp, and Guild Affiliation for workshop access and assistance. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Pirate Background
entries.summary: Kaysender pirates are former or current sky raiders whose reputations carry weight among smugglers, outlaw ports, and crews of the Black Fleet.
body: Pirates plunder airships, evade authorities, and survive through dangerous freedom. Some serve [[black-fleet|the Black Fleet]], while others belong to independent crews with their own rivalries and safe harbors.
A pirate's deeds produce a recognizable reputation among raiders, smugglers, and outlaw settlements. The same hunger for danger, treasure, and the open skies can also lure them into obvious traps.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Athletics and Deception, airship vehicles, navigator's tools, pirate clothing, a raid trophy, rope, 8 gp, and Raider's Reputation for recognition and safe harbor. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Homesteader Background
entries.summary: Homesteaders survive on remote floating islands through farming, foraging, animal care, practical tools, and stubborn self-reliance.
body: Homesteaders build lives on remote floating islands through work, resourcefulness, and perseverance. They understand local water, food, plants, animals, weather, and the practical labor needed to keep an isolated household alive.
They are proud of making things with their own hands and fiercely protective of home and family, though independence can harden into stubbornness and reluctance to seek help.

sections.heading: Legacy Background Package
body: The source grants Survival and Animal Handling, herbalism and carpenter's or brewer's tools, an axe or hoe, charm, seeds or herbs, 5 gp, and Island Survivalist for locating water, food, and dangerous flora or fauna. Conversion is required.
